findings.description: The EC2 instance's user_data script embeds a long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key in cleartext. Instance user data is readable via the EC2 metadata service and API to anyone with instance/API access, and these static credentials grant whatever privileges the key holds.

Port 22 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH on the portal server to brute-force and exploitation from the entire internet; combined with the instance's public subnet and public IP this is directly reachable.
Egress allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, so a compromised instance can exfiltrate data and reach arbitrary external hosts, including the embedded credentials and any attached EBS data.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances launched here automatically receive public IP addresses and are internet-reachable, removing the network boundary around the portal server.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so any instance launched in this subnet is automatically given a public IP and exposed to the internet.
The route table routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the internet gateway and is associated with both subnets, making the portal subnet public and enabling direct inbound/outbound internet traffic to the instance.

The EBS data volume attached to the portal server has no encrypted setting, so data written to the disk (which also holds credentials-bearing instance state) is stored unencrypted and readable from snapshots.
The EBS snapshot of the server disk is created without encryption, so a copy of the unencrypted disk contents can be shared or accessed outside the encryption boundary.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, so the web service is reachable from the entire internet over cleartext HTTP with no restriction to trusted networks.

findings.issue_category: flow logs delivered to unencrypted bucket
findings.description: The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configured, so network traffic metadata (including internal addressing and traffic patterns) is stored unencrypted.
